clue.text: See 23
Lounge and look at sport, turned over to follow golf score

indicators.note: to follow puts the look-and-sport pieces after the golf score

parts.note: par is the standard score for a golf hole
lo is an old word meaning look, see

indicators.note: turned over says the sport's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A golf fan relaxes and watches sport after reporting a round score.
explanation.definitionFit: A parlour is a sitting room, a synonym for a lounge in a house.

clue.text: Tungsten and lead club

parts.note: W is the chemical symbol for tungsten
an edge is a lead or advantage, as in having the edge

explanation.surface: A metal-and-lead golf club described by its materials.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a golf club with a steeply angled face for lofted shots.

clue.text: Left nets caught up

indicators.note: nets means takes in or captures, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: left as in departed, went out
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A left-sided player scores a goal and the crowd is roused.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up, as in worked up or keyed up, means being in a state of agitation or thrill.

clue.text: Beautiful perfume and diamonds both reduced

indicators.note: both reduced says each of the two words loses its last letter

parts.note: a scent is a perfume
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A lovely gift of perfume and jewels, both marked down in price.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenic view is a beautiful one, so the adjective fits a lovely landscape.

clue.text: See 19
Off tee, Norman gets distance

indicators.note: off means out of order or wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Greg Norman, playing from the tee, hits a long drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Greg Norman is an Australian golfer, which suits the golf theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanometre is a tiny unit of length, a billionth of a metre, so it measures a distance.

clue.text: Rest to enter competition to make big bucks

indicators.note: to enter says the resting word goes inside the competition

parts.note: a cup is a competition with a trophy
to lean is to rest against something

explanation.surface: A golfer takes a break, then enters a tournament to win big prize money.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up is an idiom for making a large profit or winning a lot of money.

clue.text: Rough grassland: side which might go on greens?

definitions.note: a phrase defining a noun: something put on salad leaves

indicators.note: rough suggests something roughly handled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer's view of the rough grass bordering the putting greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' and 'greens' look like golf terms; here greens are salad vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing is poured over salad leaves, which are greens in the vegetable sense.

clue.text: Couples playing golf? Female left

definitions.note: Fred Couples is an American golfer, so his first name is the Couples who plays golf

parts.note: red means left-wing politically

explanation.surface: Pairs out on the golf course, with a woman leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couples' looks like pairs of people but is the surname of US golfer Fred Couples.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred is the first name of Couples the golfer, a Masters champion.

clue.text: Converts pounds and euros to cut taxes

indicators.note: to cut says the money letters are inserted into the word for converts

parts.note: to convert something is to change it
L is the abbreviation for pound, doubled for the plural
E is short for euro

explanation.surface: Someone changes money from sterling to euros to reduce their tax bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax someone is to test or strain them, and to challenge means the same.

clue.text: Warning shouts at the first from Tiger Woods

parts.note: fore is the shout golfers give to warn of a ball heading toward people

indicators.note: the first from picks the opening letter of the word Tiger

explanation.surface: Golfers shout warnings at the opening hole, prompted by Tiger Woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woods' looks like part of Tiger Woods's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is a large area of trees, which is what woods are.

clue.text: American bar with players — tense meeting at the end

parts.note: but means except, as does bar
men are players in a team or on a board
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An American drinking spot full of players hosts a fraught meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An abutment is where two things meet end to end, a point of contact or junction.

clue.text: Golf? Managed two days with terribly sad old men

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to run something is to manage it
D is the abbreviation for day, here twice

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters of sad are disordered

explanation.surface: Elderly men glumly manage a couple of days of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandfathers are typically elderly men, so the plural fits old men.

clue.text: Club close to tee on hole

parts.note: nigh means near or close to
T is spelt as tee
a hole is a tight spot or predicament

explanation.surface: A golfer picks a club when the tee is near the hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a golf club; it is a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot is a nightclub or venue for evening entertainment.

clue.text: Pack up trophies in retirement

indicators.note: in retirement suggests going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pots are slang for cups or trophies

explanation.surface: A retired champion boxes up their trophies.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack up is to stop or finish, as when a machine packs up.

clue.text: John Daly finally has something to fear

parts.note: john and bog are both slang for a toilet

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word Daly

explanation.surface: Golfer John Daly at last faces a frightening prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: John Daly is an American golfer; here John is slang for a lavatory. A bogey is also a golf score.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogy, or bogey, is a bugbear or object of dread.

clue.text: Land ball at the back, stand to welcome American

indicators.note: to welcome says the stand word takes in the picked letter

parts.note: to bear is to stand or tolerate

indicators.note: at the back picks the end letter of the word ball

explanation.surface: A golfer lands the ball at the back of the green, and the grandstand greets a US player.
explanation.definitionFit: Belarus is a country, a land in Eastern Europe.

clue.text: Right, take in lead on second shot?

parts.note: to eat is to take in food
to tempt someone is to lead them on

explanation.surface: A golfer, told to take a lead on the second shot, plays it right.
explanation.definitionFit: A further try at something is a second shot, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Tiger gutted over short 19 5 round: something on fairway?

indicators.note: over in a down answer places the first piece above the second
gutted means the inside letters of the word Tiger are removed
round says the shortened colour is turned backwards
short says the colour loses its final letter

parts.note: the answer to 19 and 5 together is a primary colour, here yellow

explanation.surface: Tiger, gutted after a round, eyes something on the fairway.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow is one of the 19 5 (primary colours) that mix with blue to make green.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf trolley is a wheeled cart for clubs pulled along the fairway.

clue.text: Rory McIlroy nearly up a shot — like either of two that make green?

definitions.text: like either of two that make green?

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are rearranged
nearly says the golfer's name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Rory McIlroy is almost one stroke ahead on the green.
explanation.walkthrough: Rory McIlroy is a Northern Irish golfer. 'Green' looks like the putting surface; it is the paint colour made from blue and yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue and yellow are the two paints that mix to make green, and each is a basic paint shade in that system.

clue.text: American player, Tom, to progress smoothly

definitions.meaning: An American actor, a player on screen
to move along steadily and easily, like a car at speed

explanation.surface: A US golfer named Tom moves easily through the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests a golfer, but it is an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Cruise is a Hollywood actor, and to cruise is to travel along with ease.

clue.text: Clubs turned on men — is private part for woman?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
lit means switched on
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A golfer turns his clubs on the men, asking whether a part of the course is for women only.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female genital organ, so an intimate body part of a woman.

clue.text: Plant fruit trees here? One for middle of park

indicators.note: for says one piece stands in place of another

parts.note: an orchard is a place where fruit trees grow

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letters of the word park

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to plant fruit trees in the middle of a park.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, often exotic and prized.

clue.text: It spices up Ryder Cup: row turns nasty

indicators.note: turns nasty suggests things going wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dispute at the Ryder Cup gets ugly and livens up the contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ryder Cup is the golf match between Europe and the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: This spice blend is used to add heat and flavour to dishes.

clue.text: Ian Poulter upset about an outburst

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: relating to an eruption

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Golfer Ian Poulter is upset and loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Poulter is an English golfer known for his Ryder Cup passion.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to an eruption, which is a violent outburst.

clue.text: In Baltimore a player makes cut

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A golfer in Baltimore makes the cut in a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes cut' looks like the golf term for qualifying for the final rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut a crop such as grain at harvest.

clue.text: Place to rest?

parts.note: to set something is to place it
a tee is the little peg on which a golf ball rests before being driven

explanation.surface: A simple question about where to sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as golf, 'place' then 'rest' are setting the ball on its peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa, a piece of furniture for sitting and resting on.

clue.text: Opposition regularly says "guys": unknown Yankee interrupts

indicators.note: interrupts says the pair of letters breaks into the picked letters
regularly picks every other letter of the two quoted words

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An opponent keeps saying 'guys' until an anonymous American cuts in.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy it is the alignment of three bodies, which includes opposition and conjunction.
